posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Ah okay, got it.

Well that is subjective and depends on how familiar you are with linux. It comes with practice.

For me it looks glaringly obvious that (b), (c), and (d) are incorrect options, the more you use these tools (and redirections) and more you understand how it works. In the end it has a deterministic behavior so there’s no guessing involved.

Reasoning:

b: If we move 2>&1 after the pipe, it is not capturing stderr of the command, it is stderr of tee, which we don’t want.
c: If you use > redirection in LHS of pipe, then RHS of pipe will get no input so the tee does nothing, it would also overwrite the file with empty data.
d: same here.

a works because:

  • both stderr and stdout are merged to stdout (we want both, so good)
  • | takes the stdout (that contains stderr msgs too) to tee
  • tee prints both to screen and also saves to file.
